title: Flutter cuts 1,400 jobs, blaming UK betting tax rises
title_zh: Flutter宣布裁员1400人，怪英国博彩税上涨

image.credit: Photo by DANSHEN SOMINTAC on Unsplash
image.author: DANSHEN SOMINTAC

lead: The owner of Paddy Power is shedding up to 1,400 jobs, saying it cannot absorb higher gambling taxes. The company warns the tax burden is reshaping the UK betting market.

paragraphs: Flutter Entertainment, the gambling giant behind Paddy Power, Sky Bet and Betfair, has unveiled plans to cut as many as 1,400 jobs, with its boss insisting the company "cannot fully absorb" the tax rises levied on the gambling industry. Staff in Leeds and Dublin, along with UK and Ireland business employees at Flutter's Portugal and Romania sites, stand to be hardest hit, though the company has not disclosed which roles are at risk.

The government announced the tax increases on online casino and sports betting, with an exemption for horse racing, in last year's Budget. Kevin Harrington, chief executive of Flutter's UK and Ireland business, argued the hikes had "fundamentally changed" the economic model of the industry and had helped "fuel the unlicensed, unregulated market". Flutter expects the increases to have "a very significant impact on the overall market".

Flutter, which employs 28,500 people worldwide including 9,000 in the UK and Ireland, could also see cuts affect staff in London, Sunderland, Malta and Gibraltar, the BBC understands. Harrington said: "As we warned a year ago, we cannot fully absorb a rise of this magnitude without reducing our fixed cost base." A government spokesperson called the cuts "a commercial decision for Flutter, not the UK government".

Remote gaming duty rose from 21% to 40% in April, while general betting duty is set to climb from 15% to 25% online next April. Betting firms had warned of job losses and shop closures, but MPs dismissed the warnings as "scaremongering". Flutter, which delisted from the London Stock Exchange in August and now trades solely in New York, reported a $299m pre-tax loss for the three months to June, despite sales rising 3% to $4.3bn.

The restructuring is expected to cost between $80m and $90m. Flutter has previously estimated that the UK tax rises would dent its underlying profit by $320m this year and $540m in 2027, before any savings or restructuring. The announcement follows similar moves across the sector, with Ladbrokes owner Entain cutting roles over the summer.
paragraphs_zh: 博彩巨头Flutter Entertainment旗下拥有Paddy Power、Sky Bet和Betfair，如今宣布最多裁员1400人。公司老板坚称，面对博彩业加税，公司“无法完全消化”这部分成本。利兹和都柏林的员工，以及在Flutter葡萄牙和罗马尼亚站点工作的英国及爱尔兰业务员工，预计受冲击最大，但公司尚未透露哪些岗位面临风险。
英国政府在去年的预算案中宣布对在线赌场和体育博彩加税，赛马则获豁免。Flutter英国及爱尔兰业务首席执行官凯文·哈林顿认为，加税“从根本上改变”了行业的经济模式，还助长了“无牌照、不受监管的市场”。Flutter预计这些增税将对“整个市场产生非常重大的影响”。
据BBC了解，Flutter在全球拥有2.85万名员工，其中英国和爱尔兰有9000人，此次裁员还可能波及伦敦、桑德兰、马耳他和直布罗陀的员工。哈林顿表示：“正如我们一年前所警告的，不削减固定成本基础，我们就无法完全消化如此大幅的上涨。”政府发言人则称此次裁员是“Flutter的商业决定，而非英国政府的决定”。
远程博彩税已于4月从21%上调至40%，而一般博彩税预计明年4月在线部分将从15%升至25%。博彩公司此前曾警告会裁员、关店，但议员们斥之为“危言耸听”。Flutter今年8月从伦敦证券交易所退市，目前仅在纽约交易；截至6月的三个月里，公司税前亏损2.99亿美元，尽管销售额增长3%至43亿美元。
此次重组预计耗资8000万至9000万美元。Flutter此前估算，英国加税将在今年使其基础利润减少3.2亿美元，2027年减少5.4亿美元，这还未计入任何节省或重组措施。这一消息紧随行业内的类似动向，Ladbrokes的母公司Entain已在夏季裁减岗位。
